depth.label: Projected 2027 starters

lineup.name: Miguel Amaya
lineup.note: Starter by default. Joey Bart is the likely partner, and Owen Ayers could take over by midseason. Kelly is the last starting catcher on the market, but the Cubs won't give a catcher three years (Trueblood, Nov. 25).

lineup.name: Michael Busch
lineup.note: 106 OPS+. First base was the only position where the Cubs had negative DRS.

lineup.name: Alex Bregman
lineup.note: Year 2 of 5 years, $175M. Won his second Gold Glove Sunday, the first Cubs third baseman to win since Ron Santo.

lineup.name: Open
lineup.note: Jordan Bastian (MLB.com) has Shaw as the front-runner for the remaining outfield at-bats now that Sato is in, with Ramírez in a utility or DH role. Trueblood (Nov. 25) floats both as trade chips for a Yankees starter. Alcántara is out of options.

lineup.name: Pete Crow-Armstrong
lineup.note: 2026 NL MVP, unanimous (30 of 30 first-place votes). 6-year, $115M extension starts in 2027. Platinum Glove: +26 OAA led baseball.

lineup.name: Teruaki Sato
lineup.note: Signed Nov. 25 (official): six years, $120M. 2026 Central League Triple Crown: .306/.383/.609, 39 HR, 106 RBI. A third baseman in Japan; expected in a corner outfield spot.

lineup.name: Open
lineup.note: Conforto is a free agent. Adams (MLBTR) lists him and Tyrone Taylor as likely 'modest veteran' reunions if Suzuki and Happ both leave.

Still one starter short before Dec. 1: Griffin and Peterson signed elsewhere Wednesday, so Itoh and Nick Martinez are the names left from the Cubs' list. Kelly unlikely back. Brown (neck surgery) out until about midseason.

rotation.name: Trevor Rogers

rotation.name: Edward Cabrera
rotation.note: Under control. 5.96 ERA in 2026. Hawkins wouldn't promise him a spot: 'Got to get some outs out of him.'

rotation.name: Justin Steele

rotation.name: Open
rotation.note: One more before the lockout. Griffin (Guardians) and Peterson (Rockies) signed elsewhere Wednesday. Itoh and Martinez are left from Trueblood's list; King may be headed back to San Diego. Trade idea: Will Warren from the Yankees (Trueblood).

rotation.name: Open
rotation.note: Assad (3.63 ERA, 4.92 FIP), Jordan Wicks and Braxton Garrett until Steele proves healthy or Brown returns around midseason.

Shelby Miller

lastSummary: The Padres finished a two-game sweep with a 4-1 win at Petco. Kevin Gausman lasted 3 1/3 innings and took the loss, and Daniel Palencia gave up the back-breaking hit to Gavin Sheets. Bregman and Crow-Armstrong went a combined 0-for-15 with eight strikeouts in the series, and the highest-scoring offense in baseball managed one run in 18 innings.
parkNote: Wrigley has played slightly pitcher-friendly overall (96 run factor, 2024-26) while boosting homers (106). The Cubs posted an .789 OPS at home and .747 on the road.
preview: Second starter, now: Griffin is gone (Guardians, 3 yr, $48M; Murray, confirmed by Rosenthal) and Peterson is gone (Rockies, 2 yr, $32M; Passan). Of Trueblood's three names, Itoh and Nick Martinez are left. The call: get Itoh done this weekend at the latest. Waiting now means picking from Holmes, Mahle and Boyd.

Michael King: the Padres are 'closing in' on at least one of the top remaining starters (Kevin Acee, Union-Tribune, via Padres Mission). If that's King, the top of the market is done and the Cubs' bigger add after the lockout becomes a trade.

Trade route: Trueblood floats Matt Shaw (or Pedro Ramírez) to the Yankees for Will Warren, with Ryan McMahon's $16M thrown in. New York lost Bohm to Kansas City (2 yr, $20M) Wednesday and still needs a third baseman. Worth a call.
Catcher and the clock: Kelly is still unsigned and Gary Sánchez went to Miami (1 yr, $6.5M). The CBA expires Dec. 1 at 11:59 p.m. ET, and MLB sued the union Wednesday to protect the lockout.

stats.label: Rogers (5 yr) and Sato (6 yr), both officially signed Nov. 25 (MLB transactions).
Cubs-linked starters who signed elsewhere Wednesday: Griffin (CLE, 3/$48M), Gausman (DET, 1/$25M), Peterson (COL, 2/$32M).

items.name: Crow-Armstrong: record $3.5M from the pre-arb bonus pool
items.detail: Figures finalized Wednesday by MLB and the union: $3,548,994, the most in the pool's history, topping Skenes' $3,436,343 from last year (AP, via ESPN). His three-year pool total is $5,097,329, more than double his $2,282,186 in salary from 2024-26. Misiorowski was second ($3.16M). The pool is $50M a year; MLB proposes $65M in 2027, the union $180M.
items.call: Deserved, and it costs the Cubs nothing: the pool is league money. It's also the cleanest exhibit in the union's case before Tuesday. His $10M-a-year extension starts in 2027.
Right to let him go at $25M. His xFIP said he was better than the ERA, but one year at that price is for teams with no other options. That's the next shoe for the Cubs if Itoh goes elsewhere.
items.detail: Agreed Nov. 25, pending a physical (Jeff Passan, ESPN). 35, turns 36 in January. 9-12, 4.51 ERA, 184 K in 177 2/3 innings across 32 starts for Toronto and the Cubs in 2026; 4.83 ERA in nine Cubs starts, then three runs in 3 1/3 innings in the Wild Card loss. The only pitcher with 30-plus starts every season since 2021 (MLB.com). Toronto had 'mutual' interest in a reunion (Nicholson-Smith).
items.name: Kevin Gausman (signed, Tigers: 1 yr, $25M)

items.call: Make the call. A controllable 156-inning starter for a third baseman blocked by Bregman is exactly the trade the Cubs need. Taking McMahon's money is fine if it gets it done.
items.detail: Matthew Trueblood (North Side Baseball, Nov. 25): with Bohm gone to Kansas City, the Yankees still need a righty-hitting third baseman. He proposes Shaw (or Pedro Ramírez) plus a low-level prospect for RHP Will Warren, with New York dumping Ryan McMahon's $16M for 2027. Warren, 28 next June, made 32 appearances (29 starts) and 156 innings in 2026, is controlled through 2030 and still has options.
items.name: Matt Shaw for Will Warren (trade idea, Yankees)

items.call: Nothing here is a Cubs target. Bohm leaving the Yankees without a third baseman is the one that matters, because it makes Shaw a trade chip.
items.detail: Alec Bohm agreed with Kansas City for two years, $20M (Feinsand, MLB.com). Luis Robert Jr. returns to the Orioles on one year, $12M (Heyman), after Baltimore declined his $20M option. Gary Sánchez to the Marlins, one year, $6.5M. JoJo Romero to the Padres, three years, $21M.
items.name: Bohm to the Royals; Robert back to Baltimore; Sánchez to Miami

items.call: Treat Dec. 1 as a hard wall and assume a long winter. Whatever the Cubs don't buy by Tuesday may not be buyable until March.
items.detail: MLB filed suit Wednesday in federal court in Manhattan asking a judge to declare the coming lockout legal under antitrust law, aiming to head off a union disclaimer. It names the MLBPA and the eight players on its executive subcommittee, including Tarik Skubal (ESPN; Front Office Sports). The union called it 'completely frivolous.' The CBA expires Dec. 1 at 11:59 p.m. ET.
items.name: MLB sues the union before the lockout

items.call: Losing Griffin stings less than it looks: $16M a year for three years of a 91-mph lefty is full price. Martinez on one year is fine. Two years is the limit at 36.
items.detail: Nov. 25: the Cubs were in on both, along with Itoh (Trueblood, North Side Baseball). That night Griffin agreed to return to Cleveland for three years and $48M, pending a physical (Robert Murray, FanSided, first; Ken Rosenthal confirmed). 31, 15-6, 3.60 ERA, 158 K in 172 2/3 innings in 2026; 5.19 ERA in nine starts after the trade. Martinez, 36, threw 180 innings for the pennant-winning Rays and started Game 1 of the World Series. Toronto also has him on its list (Nicholson-Smith, Sportsnet).
items.name: Nick Martinez (free agent); Foster Griffin (signed, Guardians: 3 yr, $48M)

items.call: Pay the third year. The market just emptied: Jeffers took the QO and Stephenson went home. Refusing three years on principle leaves Amaya and Bart as the starting pair, and that's the weakest spot on the roster.
items.detail: Nov. 25: the Cubs are interested in a reunion but reluctant to give any catcher three years, so a return is unlikely (Trueblood, North Side Baseball). A rival exec says a three-year deal 'is out there for him'; the Angels, Yankees and Giants could go there. He's now the top catcher left after Stephenson re-signed with the Reds (SI). The Cubs had interest in Stephenson before he took three years, $30M from Cincinnati. Kelly: 97 OPS+ and 1.9 bWAR in 2026, .871 OPS vs. lefties. Nov. 25: Gary Sánchez, the other veteran bat-first catcher, signed with Miami (1 yr, $6.5M). Cubbies Crib's Jordan Campbell argues the Cubs are right to let Kelly go a year early.
items.name: Carson Kelly (free agent)

items.call: The Cubs wanted him and wouldn't go to three years. That's the same line that will cost them Kelly. Wrong line for this market.
items.detail: Agreed Nov. 24, pending a physical, with an opt-out after the second year (Passan, ESPN; Feinsand, MLB.com). 30; .241, 15 HR, 101 OPS+, career-high 2.5 bWAR in 2026; won 68% of his ABS challenges. The Cubs had interest (Trueblood, North Side Baseball).
items.name: Tyler Stephenson (re-signed, Reds: 3 yr, $30M)

items.call: Fair for a righty bench outfielder coming off a career year. The Cubs had Shaw and Ramírez for those at-bats anyway. Fine to let him go.
items.detail: Agreed Nov. 24 (Heyman first; Feinsand had the terms). .279/.325/.502, 11 HR, 128 OPS+ in 97 games for the Mets and Cubs; .351 with a 144 OPS+ in 30 games after the August trade. .921 OPS against lefties. His xwOBA (.309) and xSLG (.416) sat well under the results (South Side Sox).
items.name: Tyrone Taylor (signed, White Sox: 2 yr, $17M)

items.call: Nothing here touches the Cubs. Seager moving would pull Philadelphia's money into the infield instead of the arms the Cubs want.
items.detail: Corey Seager is willing to waive his no-trade clause for Philadelphia, which is open to moving Trea Turner off shortstop (NBC Sports Philadelphia, via CBS). He's owed $155M through 2031. The Tigers and Ha-Seong Kim agreed to one year, $5M (Passan). The Mets may add a short-term starter after Skubal (The Athletic, via CBS).
items.name: Seager open to the Phillies; Ha-Seong Kim to Detroit

items.call: Good deal, and the deferrals make it a little better. The best lefty left at 29, for about the MLBTR number. The picks hurt but they're the price of the top tier. B+ now. It becomes an A only if a second starter follows by Dec. 1.
items.detail: Officially signed Nov. 25 (MLB transactions), two days after agreeing. Agreed late Nov. 23. Jon Morosi (MLB Network) was first; Ken Rosenthal (The Athletic) confirmed and reported five years, $120M, a $24M AAV; Jesse Rogers (ESPN) and Jordan Bastian (MLB.com) confirmed. MLBTR had projected five years, $115M; The Athletic four years, $84M. He rejected Baltimore's $23.15M QO, so the Cubs forfeit their second- and fifth-highest 2027 picks and $1M in international pool money (ESPN). 2026: 10-11, 4.03 ERA, 169 2/3 innings over 30 starts, his first 30-start season. 6.84 ERA through May after a bout of the flu, then a 2.90 ERA and 2.89 FIP over his last 20 starts. 1.81 ERA in 18 starts in 2025. Fastball back up to 93.8 mph from 91.9 in 2024 after a Driveline rework; hitters are at .204 against it since 2025. 5.6% walk rate, 92nd percentile (MLB.com). Toronto had shown interest the same day (Nicholson-Smith). Nov. 24: Jeff Passan (ESPN) says the deal includes deferrals that bring the net present value down slightly. Baltimore gets a compensatory pick (Kubatko, MASN). It's the third-largest deal ever for a Cubs pitcher, behind Jon Lester ($155M) and Yu Darvish ($126M) (CBS). Sportsnet's David Singh calls it above market: Nicholson-Smith had predicted four years, $100M. The White Sox, Padres and Braves were among the other suitors. 2026 on Baseball-Reference: 101 ERA+, 2.2 bWAR.
items.name: Trevor Rogers (signed, Cubs: 5 yr, $120M)

items.call: Free depth for a pen with almost no lefties. It costs nothing. It's not the bullpen fix.
items.detail: Agreed Nov. 24, minor-league deal with an invite to big-league camp (Jon Heyman, NY Post, via MLBTR). Lefty reliever, 34, turns 35 in January; 65 appearances for the Reds in 2026. Garrett and Jordan Wicks are the only other lefty relief options on the 40-man (MLBTR). Thielbar just left for Kansas City.
items.name: Sam Moll (minor-league deal, spring invite)

items.call: That's the one-year bounce-back price now: $17.5M. Another SP5 option the Cubs didn't take, and it makes Peterson on two years look cheap.
items.detail: Agreed Nov. 24 (Rosenthal, via Yahoo). 29, a one-year reset after only 55 innings in 2026 around elbow trouble; 2.98 ERA and a 25.5% strikeout rate over 217 1/3 innings since 2023.
items.name: Kris Bubic (signed, Guardians: 1 yr, $17.5M)

items.call: Five years for a 30-year-old coming off a 4.42 ERA. Baltimore paid for October. The Cubs were right not to go there, but they lost an arm off a short list.
items.detail: Agreed Nov. 24, five years and $125M (Rosenthal, The Athletic); Baltimore announced it the same day. $10M signing bonus and $23M a year, the biggest deal ever for an Orioles pitcher (MLB.com). Reigning ALCS MVP: 0.75 ERA over 12 innings against Cleveland. 2026: 5-9, 4.99 ERA in 22 Mets starts, then 5-2 with a 3.25 ERA in 10 for Tampa Bay (Yahoo). The Cubs had held 'extensive talks' (Nightengale, Nov. 23).
items.name: Freddy Peralta (signed, Orioles: 5 yr, $125M)

items.call: This was the one to get, and the Cubs lost him. Fair price, too: $16M a year with an opt-out. It's the biggest miss of the winter so far.
items.detail: Agreed Nov. 24: five years, $80M with an opt-out after the third season and a $5M signing bonus (Passan, via Japan Times; Feinsand, MLB.com). 27, a 1.36 ERA over 146 innings for Seibu in 2026, best in NPB; fastball touches 99. Toronto plans to use him as a starter but won't push his pitch counts (MLB.com). The Cubs had made a video-conference pitch (Mooney, The Athletic).
items.name: Kaima Taira (signed, Blue Jays: 5 yr, $80M)

items.call: Right player, right price. A 27-year-old with real power for $20M a year is the Suzuki replacement with five extra years of runway. The contact rate is the risk, and the Cubs' 21.1% team strikeout rate can absorb it. A-. It also means Suzuki is gone, and that's fine.
items.detail: Officially signed Nov. 25 (MLB transactions). Agreed Nov. 24. Michael Cerami (Bleacher Nation) first reported it was being finalized; Jeff Passan (ESPN) had the terms; Mark Feinsand (MLB.com) and Ken Rosenthal (The Athletic) confirmed. It landed about 12 hours after Rogers. 27, a two-time Central League MVP and the 2026 Triple Crown winner: .306/.383/.609, 39 HR, 106 RBI in 143 games for Hanshin; 40 homers and a .924 OPS in 2025 (NBC Sports). .271/.337/.514 with 163 homers over six NPB seasons (Blue Jays Nation). Expected to play a corner outfield spot; FanGraphs' depth chart has him in right (North Side Baseball). The risks: a 66% contact rate against a 77% MLB average (CBS), a 17.3% swinging-strike rate, second-highest among qualified NPB hitters, and a nearly 36% chase rate (NBC Sports). The posting fee to Hanshin comes on top of the $120M. Tom Verducci (MLB Network) called him 'the best bat on the market' because of his age (via Heavy).
items.name: Teruaki Sato (signed, Cubs: 6 yr, $120M)

items.call: Still the best arm on the board, and Rogers makes him a luxury instead of a necessity. Revisit after the lockout. Don't take on Devers or Adames money to get him.
items.detail: Robert Murray (FanSided, Nov. 21): the Giants are 'open to listening' on Webb, per multiple rival executives, after refusing to engage before the deadline (via MLB.com). 30, three-time All-Star; signed through 2028 with $47M left (FanSided). 2026: 4.31 ERA, 3.45 FIP, 160 1/3 innings in 27 starts with IL stints for knee bursitis and a blister. 3.19 ERA over 968 innings in 2021-25 (Heavy). FanSided ranks the Cubs the No. 1 fit; Bleacher Nation names Shaw or Ramírez as the kind of piece it takes. Nov. 22: Rosenthal and Sammon (The Athletic, via RealGM and Yahoo) say the Giants want a 'very strong return' and some rival executives doubt they'll get it. Fits named: Orioles, Blue Jays, Mets, White Sox, Braves and Cubs; a deal inside the NL West looks unlikely. San Francisco would rather move Devers, Adames or Chapman. $23M in 2027, $24M in 2028 (Heavy). Nov. 23: Just Baseball calls him the best fit available, a true No. 1 with a 3.35 ERA since 2021 and the most innings in the majors over that span, but warns the prospect cost could push the Cubs to free agency. Last Word on Sports notes no team has been formally linked yet. Nov. 23 evening: Nightengale (USA Today) says 'several executives' think the Giants' best shot at moving Adames, Chapman or Devers is a package that also sends Webb, and a deal of that size is 'doubtful' before the CBA expires Dec. 1, though San Francisco 'could certainly line something up' for later (via MLB.com).
items.name: Logan Webb (trade, Giants)

items.call: Headed back to San Diego, by the look of it. Fine. Don't chase him past four years.
items.detail: Nov. 24: MLB.com calls him 'likely the best starting pitcher still available' after Rogers, Peralta and Taira signed, with 'a handful of clubs in the mix,' the Cubs and Mets among those linked. Declined his player option. 3.21 ERA in 185 innings, but 21.0% K and 9.2% BB were career worsts (FanGraphs). Morosi (Nov. 13) called King-Cubs a 'pairing that many of us have forecasted'; on Nov. 20 he said the White Sox are in on King too (MLB.com). MLBTR projects four years, $92M. Morosi (Nov. 20) thinks King and Peralta won't sign until after Skubal decides (MLB.com). Nov. 22: MLB.com's AJ Cassavell calls King San Diego's 'most obvious pivot' after missing on Skubal; Preller has said there's 'a lot of interest' in a reunion, and King wants to return. Nov. 23: Nightengale says the Padres will 'do everything possible to bring back' King; they're also eyeing a Pivetta reunion. Toronto is interested too (Nicholson-Smith, via MLBTR). Nov. 25: Trueblood (North Side Baseball) says King, Mahle and Holmes may be priced past the Cubs' appetite after Rogers. MLB.com's belief is King signs with one of his suitors by the end of the week. Nov. 25: the Padres are 'closing in on a deal with at least one of the top remaining starting pitchers,' with King at the top of the list (Kevin Acee, San Diego Union-Tribune, via Padres Mission). Morosi 'wholeheartedly' expects him to sign by the end of the week (MLB.com).
items.name: Michael King (free agent)

items.call: Gone, and that's the right outcome now. Sato is five years younger at a lower AAV. Take the comp pick.
items.detail: Nov. 24: Sato's deal 'effectively replaces' Suzuki (FanSided). Jon Morosi (MLB Network) calls Suzuki and Toronto 'as clean and clear a fit as there is,' with at-bats in the corner outfield and at DH (via Heavy). Passan (ESPN): San Diego met with Suzuki on Monday and may be the favorite (via MLB.com, Nov. 18). The Padres also lost seven starters and are meeting Skubal Wednesday. Nov. 21: Mike Petriello (MLB.com) finds Suzuki and Arozarena with identical four-year lines (14 fWAR, about 30% better than average) and leans Suzuki on bat speed (63rd percentile), chase (89th) and a +7 FRV year in right. Red flag: his hard-hit rate fell 10 points, a top-five drop. Nov. 23: Toronto is focusing on its lineup after Skubal and has been linked to Suzuki, Arozarena, Sato, Brandon Lowe and Jazz Chisholm Jr. (Bannon, The Athletic, via MLB.com).
items.name: Padres, Blue Jays chase Suzuki

items.call: None of it touches the Cubs directly, but the Sato line matters: once he signs, Toronto's lineup money is spent and it can turn to the same arms the Cubs want. Get Peralta done before that happens.
items.detail: Nov. 23: the Mets signed Paul Goldschmidt for one year and $8M plus $2M in incentives (Murray, Sammon, Sherman, via MLBTR); he hit .299/.393/.573 against lefties in 2026 and .213/.239/.351 against righties. The Yankees signed lefty reliever Brent Suter for one year, $4M with a 2028 club option (Passan, via Heavy). Rosenthal hears Teruaki Sato could sign 'very well before Thanksgiving'; Feinsand says the Yankees, Phillies and Blue Jays are the frontrunners (MLB.com).
items.name: Goldschmidt to the Mets; Suter to the Yankees; Sato could sign before Thanksgiving

items.call: Fine. Declining the option was right and nothing here changes it.
items.detail: Agreed Nov. 23 (Jorge Castillo, ESPN, via RotoBaller). Turns 40 in January. 4.86 ERA in 58 games and 50 innings for the Cubs in 2026, with 60 strikeouts, 18 walks and a career-high 11 homers allowed. The Cubs declined his option this month.
items.name: Caleb Thielbar (signed, Royals: 1 yr, $3.25M)

items.call: Gone, and fine. A reclamation flier at $2.3M was never the answer. It does show how fast the cheap tier is clearing out.
items.detail: Agreed Sunday, one day after the Yankees non-tendered him (MLB.com; Yahoo). The Red Sox had also shown interest (Healey, Boston Globe, via MLBTR). 2026: 27 1/3 innings over nine appearances with more walks (18) than strikeouts (17), around shoulder inflammation.
items.name: Luis Gil (signed, Tigers: 1 yr, $2.3M)

items.call: Four suitors means the price goes up, not down. Let someone else pay to fix a 69 wRC+. Every Cubs chip should buy pitching first.
items.detail: Boston tendered him Friday; he isn't on MLB.com's non-tender list, so he's trade-only now. Mooney (The Athletic, Nov. 19): the Cubs evaluated him 'as a potential change-of-scenery addition.' MLBTR projects $11.1M. 76 OPS+ and .207/.266/.361 in 2026; 10.4 fWAR across 2024-25. Fox notes Boston has asked about Suzuki to replace him. Nov. 22: Cotillo and McAdam (MassLive, via MLBTR) add the Padres, Mariners and Phillies as clubs that have done due diligence; four confirmed suitors including the Cubs. 69 wRC+ and a 27.1% K rate in 2026.
items.name: Jarren Duran (trade, Red Sox)

items.call: Sitting out was right at $50M a year; nobody was getting the Cubs to that number. What matters now is the clock. Boras said the decision touched '10 to 15 pitching decisions' elsewhere. Those decisions start tonight, and the Cubs have to be first in line, not fifth.
items.detail: Agreed Sunday (Heyman, NY Post; Feinsand, MLB.com). $50M AAV, the record for a pitcher, plus a $45M signing bonus paid on signing and a no-trade clause (Nightengale, via Yahoo). It beat Toronto's nine years at just over $400M (Bannon, The Athletic); the Dodgers never made an offer (Alden González, ESPN). The Mets went from +2200 to +1300 to win the 2027 World Series at DraftKings (Fox Sports). Sharma had reported Nov. 9 that the Cubs would sit out.
items.name: Tarik Skubal (signed, Mets: 9 yr, $450M)

items.call: Not a Cubs fit with Hoerner locked in at second. It matters because every team that gets Marte stops shopping for bats the Cubs might want to move.
items.detail: Rosenthal and Sammon (The Athletic, Nov. 21): Arizona wants to cut payroll and a Marte deal looks inevitable. Orioles, Blue Jays, Red Sox and Rays are named suitors (ClutchPoints, via Murray). He has 10-and-5 rights, so he can veto. .249, 22 HR in 2026; about five years, $89M left (Yahoo).
items.name: Ketel Marte trade 'inevitable if not imminent'

items.call: France is a real option for a Cubs first base/DH platoon if Busch slips again. At $15M a year, no. The Cubs' money goes to arms.
items.detail: Sheets re-signed for three years, $11M with player options after 2027 and 2028 (MLB.com, Nov. 20). France (.295, 21 HR, .865 OPS) wants three years at $14.5M-$20M AAV, per The Athletic (via ClutchPoints, Nov. 21); the Mets, Pirates, Guardians, D-backs, Brewers and White Sox are named.
items.name: Padres keep Sheets; Ty France wants three years

items.call: Jones is a real left-field idea for a club without one, but every Cubs chip should buy pitching first. Watch, don't chase.
items.detail: The Mets agreed to an eight-year extension with the 22-year-old Ewing, control through 2035 (MLB.com). Cashman says teams are 'asking a lot' about Jones and also Jasson Domínguez (Kuty, The Athletic, via MLB.com). The Mets are also getting calls on Mark Vientos.
items.name: Mets extend A.J. Ewing; Yankees take calls on Spencer Jones and Domínguez

items.call: Three years is fine for a 29-year-old with a deep mix and real control. He's a No. 3 or 4, not the 'no-doubt' arm Sharma wants, so he can't be the last starter they add. Win the bid today.
items.detail: Nov. 25: the Cubs are bidders, sources tell Matthew Trueblood (North Side Baseball). He has multiple three-year offers and could decide as soon as Wednesday. 5-foot-9, low 90s, an exceptionally deep pitch mix and excellent control; some teams worry the MLB ball will cost his pitches movement. Earlier: visited Chicago (Castillo, ESPN); MLB.com had both Chicago clubs possibly in the mix (Nov. 24). 2025 Sawamura winner; 3.18 ERA, 159 K, 34 BB over 172 2/3 innings in 2026. MLBTR projected two years, $20M; the three-year offers already beat that.
items.name: Hiromi Itoh (NPB, posted)

items.call: Fine as the backup. Wrong if it's the Kelly replacement. Amaya plus Bart is the weakest catching pair the Cubs have run in years, and Kelly is still sitting there on a two-year deal.
items.detail: Claimed Friday (Feinsand, MLB.com) after Chicago's AL club DFA'd him Tuesday; the Cubs avoided arbitration with him, terms not disclosed (MLB.com via MLB Korea). 29, former No. 2 overall pick. .214/.305/.357, 4 HR, 82 OPS+ in 128 PA for Pittsburgh, Atlanta and the White Sox; broke his left hand Aug. 6. 120 wRC+ in 80 games for the 2024 Pirates. Last arbitration year; MLBTR had projected $2.9M.
items.name: Joey Bart (waiver claim, White Sox)

items.call: Optionable depth for Iowa. Better than another out-of-options claim. Still not pitching help.
items.detail: 27, debuted Aug. 28; 3.38 ERA over 5 1/3 MLB innings with the Giants. 3.78 ERA, 60 K, 26 BB in 64 1/3 Triple-A innings. Has minor-league options (CubsHQ). Washington had claimed him Oct. 29.
items.name: Braxton Roxby (trade, Nationals, for cash)

items.call: Right on both. The infield depth behind Swanson is now thin, so a minor-league reunion for Arias wouldn't be crazy.
items.detail: Both are free agents (MLB.com). Arias: 10 PA as a Cub after the August claim, projected $1.3M. Roberts: 4.21 ERA in 23 games in 2026, 4.70 career. Nine others tendered: Amaya, Busch, Garrett, Rolison, Steele, Assad, Brown, Cabrera, Palencia (MLB.com via MLB Korea). 40-man at 37.
items.name: Gabriel Arias, Ethan Roberts non-tendered

items.call: Larnach was on Adams' cheap-LF list, and now he costs nothing but money. Ober is a one-year rotation flier. Make calls Monday.
items.detail: Minnesota non-tendered Bailey Ober and Trevor Larnach, released Matt Wallner, and traded Lewis for Bobby Miller and a catching prospect (MLB.com). St. Louis cut Nolan Gorman; Boston cut Connor Wong. Duran and Burger were tendered.
items.name: Tender day: Ober, Larnach, Wallner, Gorman hit the market; Royce Lewis to the Dodgers

items.call: Oviedo for a Class A lefty is the kind of cheap rotation flier the Cubs should be scooping. Another one gone.
items.detail: Arizona got RHP Johan Oviedo from Boston for minor-league LHP Luke Dotson and a PTBNL or cash; he missed most of 2026 with an elbow sprain (MLB.com). Detroit extended Troy Melton six years, $46.5M guaranteed, after a 2.76 ERA in 20 starts. The Giants kept Camilo Doval for one year, reportedly $6.3M, and sent Christian Koss to the Rays.
items.name: Oviedo to Arizona, Melton extended, Doval stays in San Francisco

items.call: This is the internal-options pitch for the corners. It lines up with Hawkins' Nov. 13 comments. Fine for one spot. Not for two, and not if it means the Suzuki money never gets spent.
items.detail: Daily Herald (Nov. 20): Kelly said there's 'a version of [Busch] somewhere in between' his 2025 breakout and his 2026 drop, and the club is 'excited about Matt Shaw being healthy.' Happ, Suzuki, Kelly and Taylor are all free agents.
items.name: Hitting coach Dustin Kelly backs Busch and a healthy Shaw

items.call: Gone, and the Cubs were never on his list. That's another sinkerballer they could have had for two years. Morejon is the last impact reliever left; get in.
items.detail: Signed Friday (Jorge Castillo, ESPN, via Fox Sports). 2.42 ERA, 1.03 WHIP, 172 ERA+ over 67 innings with Arizona in 2026. MLBTR had projected two years, $13M. The Yankees also kept Tim Hill earlier (1 yr, $2.25M).
items.name: Loaisiga back to the Yankees (2 yr, club option for 2029)

items.call: Fine as a development plan, dangerous as a roster plan. A blister-prone 5.96 ERA is not one of the two arms they need. If the front office counts a fixed Cabrera as an addition, the winter already failed.
items.detail: MLB.com (Casey Drottar, Nov. 19): Hoyer said the club 'struggled with Edward' and has to own not getting the most out of him. Hawkins blamed blisters and said fixing his fingers is the priority; VP of pitching strategy Tyler Zombro checks in with him every morning. Cabrera gave the Cubs 80 innings of 5.96 ERA after costing the No. 1 prospect.
items.name: Hoyer, Hawkins: 'We have to get more out of' Cabrera

items.call: Two more mid-rotation trade arms off the board, and Colorado got them for a lefty and a catching prospect. That's the price range the Cubs should have been working in. The trade tier is thinning as fast as the free-agent tier.
items.detail: ESPN (Nov. 19): Colorado acquires right-handers Castillo and Martin; the White Sox get LHP Sean Sullivan and catching prospect Douglas Veliz. Also Nov. 19: the Royals and Randy Dobnak agreed to a one-year, $1.35M deal.
items.name: Rockies get Luis Castillo, Davis Martin from the White Sox

items.call: Free lottery ticket with a real strikeout rate, and it costs a roster spot they weren't using. Fine. Just don't let anyone count it as pitching help. Expect him back on waivers before spring.
items.detail: Claimed Thursday; Heyman had it first (MLBTR). 28, out of options, 10.18 career ERA over 20 1/3 MLB innings with Baltimore, the Dodgers and the Mets. Since 2023 in the minors: 3.99 ERA, 30.5% K, 14.6% BB over 320 innings. The Mets had signed him for 2027 and tried to slip him through waivers. No corresponding move; the 40-man is at 37.
items.name: Chayce McDermott (waiver claim, Mets)

items.call: Another bidder on the exact one-year bounce-back tier the Cubs would use to fill SP5. Bubic is the best of those bets. Make the offer before Baltimore or Washington does.
items.detail: Spencer Nusbaum (The Athletic, via MLBTR, Nov. 19): Washington prefers short free-agent deals and has asked about Kris Bubic, Brady Singer and Kona Takahashi. Bubic: 2.98 ERA and 25.5% K over 217 1/3 innings since 2023, but only 55 innings in 2026 around elbow trouble.
items.name: Nationals want short-term starters: Bubic, Singer, Takahashi

items.call: Fine to lose the player at that price for a 37-year-old with a fading fastball. Not fine that he was one of the Cubs' own linked names and nobody even reported a Cubs offer. That's three linked arms gone this week: May, Gray, and the Mariners' trade door.
items.detail: Announced Wednesday (MLBTR, Nov. 18; Heyman first had the $55M). $20M in 2027, then a $30M player option for 2028 with a $5M buyout, so it works like an opt-out after one year. 2.72 ERA over 169 innings and fifth in AL Cy Young voting, but the four-seamer fell to a career-low 91.5 mph and he allowed in-zone contact at a career-high 92.1%.
items.name: Sonny Gray to the Twins (2 yr, $55M)

items.call: That kills the Kirby-Hancock idea. Seattle wanted a third baseman and got one from Kansas City, not from the Cubs' spare young bats. The Cubs had the pieces and the need, and the Royals made the deal.
items.detail: Six players: Seattle gets 3B Maikel Garcia (five years, $57.5M, through 2030), RP James McArthur and LHP prospect L.P. Langevin; Kansas City gets Miller, Evans and LHP Jose A. Ferrer (Passan, Divish, Rosenthal via MLBTR). Dipoto told the Seattle Times there is 'zero' chance of trading another starter. Seattle's 2027 rotation: Gilbert, Woo, Kirby, Hancock and Anderson.
items.name: Mariners trade Bryce Miller, Logan Evans to the Royals; Dipoto: 'zero' chance of another starter deal

items.call: The market for the Cubs' top target just added the Mets. Rymer (Bleacher Report) already predicts Taira to the White Sox at four years, $68M. If the Cubs want him, they have to bid like it this week, not 'show interest.'
items.detail: Heyman (NY Post): the Mets set a Zoom meeting with Taira. MLBTR lists the Padres, Blue Jays and 'both Chicago clubs' as interested and says he 'will almost certainly sign in the next two weeks' (Franco, Nov. 18). Separately, Franco reports the White Sox are after another notable starter after May, naming Taira and Rogers among the options.
items.name: Mets schedule Taira; White Sox want another starter

items.call: Treat Dec. 1 as a hard wall. Anything the Cubs don't buy in the next 12 days is likely off the table until spring, and the players who sign in that window are the ones with deadlines: Taira and the QO guys.
items.detail: At the owners' meetings Wednesday: 'They want salary cap and floor, and on that, we will not compromise.' MLBPA chief Bruce Meyer called it 'a radical change to the system.' A Dec. 2 lockout is 'all but officially guaranteed' (MLBTR, Nov. 18). The last one ran 99 days.
items.name: Manfred: MLB 'will not compromise' on cap and floor

items.call: Now he's a real option, and he's the 'impact arm' Hoyer keeps promising. Five years for a reliever is too long. Three years at a higher AAV, picks and all, is worth it for a pen that blew 28 saves.
items.detail: Turned down the $23.15M offer Tuesday and wants to stay a reliever; MLB.com lists the Mets, Cubs and Giants as fits (via MLB Data Warehouse, Nov. 18). MLBTR projects five years, $80M. 99.1 mph, 30.4% K, 2.83 ERA over 86 innings. Signing him costs the Cubs two picks and $1M in pool money.
items.name: Adrian Morejon rejects the Padres' QO

items.call: Done deal, and the 'interest' line is politeness. Take the pick and don't chase him past three years. The money goes to an arm.
items.detail: Rejected the $23.15M QO Tuesday (Alden González, ESPN). .270, 26 HR, 86 RBI, .841 OPS, career-high 81 walks, +7 fielding run value in 2026 (MLB.com). MLBTR projects four years, $105M. Hawkins: 'We would be silly not to have interest in reuniting with him.' Linked to the Phillies, Blue Jays and Royals (USA Today). Comp pick lands after the fourth round. Passan: the Padres met him Monday and may be the favorite.
items.name: Seiya Suzuki

items.call: Off the board. The Cubs had the young bats Seattle wanted and let the Royals beat them to it.
items.detail: Dead. Dipoto told the Seattle Times there is 'zero' chance of trading another starter after Miller and Evans went to Kansas City for Maikel Garcia (MLBTR, Nov. 18). Kirby and Hancock are in Seattle's 2027 rotation.
items.name: George Kirby, Emerson Hancock (trade, Mariners)

items.call: Gone. Scratch him from the list.
items.detail: Signed with Minnesota Nov. 18: two years, $55M, with an effective opt-out after 2027 (MLBTR).
items.name: Sonny Gray (signed, Twins)

items.call: Triple-A depth. A 5.9 BB/9 career walk rate is not the 'impact arm' Hoyer promised.
items.detail: Announced by his agency Nov. 17; terms unknown, likely not a guaranteed deal (Cubs Insider). Career 5.34 ERA, 254 K and 146 BB in 246 innings with the Rockies, Pirates, Twins and Nationals.
items.name: Justin Lawrence (likely minor-league deal)

items.call: Deserved. It also tells you where the 2027 problem isn't. The best lineup and best defense in the NL lost a Wild Card sweep because the pitching was thin. Fix the staff.
items.detail: PCA's first, Bregman's second, and the franchise's first team Silver Slugger. Cubs Insider says they're the first team to win the team Silver Slugger and team Gold Glove in the same season.
items.name: PCA, Bregman and the team win Silver Sluggers

items.call: Fair price, and the Cubs shouldn't mourn the player. They should mourn the pace. The crosstown team is now one arm up, and $17.5M a year for a 4.70 ERA just set the floor for the Holmes-Peterson tier.
items.detail: Agreed Tuesday; agent Craig Rose confirmed $52.5M to Jon Heyman after Robert Murray's first report (MLBTR, Nov. 17). 4.70 ERA, 3.63 FIP and 3.99 SIERA over a career-high 145 2/3 innings in 2026, 96.9 mph four-seamer. Strikeout rate has sat around 21-22% since 2023.
items.name: Dustin May to the White Sox (3 yr, $52.5M)

items.call: Jeffers staying in Minnesota takes the top catcher off the board. That makes Carson Kelly the best realistic catcher add. Sign him on two years before someone else does.
items.detail: Bednar took $23.15M from the Yankees, the biggest one-year salary ever for a reliever (Hoch, MLB.com). Jeffers took the Twins' QO, reversing reports he'd decline (Gleeman). Five others rejected: Suzuki, Arozarena, Rogers, Brandon Lowe, Morejon (Alden González, ESPN, via MLBTR).
items.name: Bednar and Jeffers accept QOs

items.call: Right calls, both. Neither is a 2027 rotation answer. Wiggins was the Detmers trade chip at the deadline, so protecting him keeps that deal alive.
items.detail: Protected from the Rule 5 draft Tuesday; the 40-man is at 36 (MLBTR). Wiggins, Baseball America's No. 4 Cubs prospect: upper-90s heat, 2.19 ERA and 31% K in 2025, then a 6.75 ERA and 17.3% walk rate in 42 2/3 innings around elbow trouble in 2026. McCullough: 3.27 ERA, 27.7% K over 55 innings, mostly Double-A. Starter or reliever for Wiggins gets decided in spring.
items.name: Jaxon Wiggins, Brody McCullough added to the 40-man

items.call: Baltimore is a direct rival for Rogers and the Peterson fallback. That's two more bidders on the exact arms the Cubs are 'contacting.' Pick one and move.
items.detail: Kostka (Baltimore Banner) says Baltimore is leaning left-handed: Rogers first, then Kris Bubic and Matthew Boyd; he names Peterson as a possible fit. Robert Murray (FanSided) reports several teams are interested in Peterson (MLBTR, Nov. 16). Baltimore has $40M+ of room.
items.name: Orioles chase lefties: Rogers, Bubic, Boyd

items.call: Correct. One year as the No. 5 at most, and only after two real starters are signed.
items.detail: No QO. Declined his side of the $15M mutual option ($2M buyout). 3.91 ERA, 18.5% K rate. Turns 36 in February. The Orioles are interested (Kostka) and he's been tied to the Padres. MLBTR projects one year, $13M.
items.name: Matthew Boyd

items.call: Gone, and $16M a year is more than the Cubs should have paid. The problem is the fallback list is now Itoh, Martinez and Holmes.
items.detail: Agreed Nov. 25: two years, $32M (Jeff Passan, ESPN). 31, grew up in the Denver area. 114 ERA+ in 15 starts for the Cubs after the June trade, 4.06 FIP, 10.2% walk rate. MLBTR had projected two years, $24M. Jesse Rogers (ESPN) had him in play for the Cubs as recently as Nov. 24.
items.name: David Peterson (signed, Rockies: 2 yr, $32M)

items.call: Door closed. Two years at MLBTR's number would have been fine, but at least now it's clear. The money goes elsewhere.
items.detail: Nov. 24: Jesse Rogers (ESPN Chicago) thinks the Cubs have 'shut the door' on Imanaga after conversations earlier this offseason (via MLB.com). 112 ERA+ in 32 starts, 35 homers allowed. Not QO-eligible. Barely linked anywhere so far; Morosi named the Tigers as a possible suitor Friday (Bleacher Nation). MLBTR projects two years, $40M; FanGraphs two years, $28M.
items.name: Shota Imanaga

payroll.label: 2027 guarantees, per MLBTR (before Rogers and Sato)
Rogers' AAV (5 yr, $120M; deferrals lower the tax hit slightly, per Passan). Signed Nov. 25.
Sato's posting fee to Hanshin, by the MLB-NPB formula CBS lays out (not a tax hit)
Room under the tax threshold after both (Cubbies Crib's ~$68M, less $44M in AAV)
CBA expires (lockout all but certain Dec. 2)

stove.summary: Rogers (5 yr, $120M) and Sato (6 yr, $120M) went official Wednesday. Then the market ate the Cubs' second-starter list: Griffin to Cleveland (3 yr, $48M), Gausman to Detroit (1 yr, $25M), Peterson to Colorado (2 yr, $32M). Thanksgiving brought nothing. Itoh and Nick Martinez are left, and MLB.com's belief is King signs somewhere before the weekend is out. The call: sign Itoh before the lockout, then pay Kelly the third year. Amaya and Bart is not a contender's catching pair.
